document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: MISSION STATEMENT
evidence.content:
MISSION STATEMENT
• Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club (LWR PC) mission aims to be the premier club in
Lakewood Ranch (LWR) and Southwest Florida.
• LWR PC’s goal is to foster fair, competitive and social play within LWR and area
communities and with local players.
• LWR PC's DUPR Leagues will provide an organized and competitive play that considers the
needs of Captains and Players, adheres to rules, and maintains low costs.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
evidence.content:
1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
evidence.content:
2. CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
Each team in the League must be led by a designated Captain. That individual may also assume
the position of Co-Captain on a diƯerent team and can also serve as Captain for a team of the
opposite gender. However, an individual is not permitted to hold the role of Captain for more
than one team within the same gender category in a Division. A Captain or Co-Captain is not
required to be an active player on the team but may instead serve in a supportive capacity by
assisting with the responsibilities assigned to the Captain. For comprehensive “How to”
instructions for Captains, please consult the DUPR League Captains Guide.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
evidence.content:
3. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. All League players must have a signed/accepted waiver with LWR PC and have a valid
LWR PC membership. To sign up, go to https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup/.
3.2. All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be found at:
https://www.dupr.com/.
3.3. All DUPR League players must join our free DUPR club, which is diƯerent/separate from
the LWR PC membership: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB
3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may form teams with members from other communities; however, they are not
permitted to play for another community’s team if their own community already has a
team in their division and has roster availability for additional players.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
3.6. Captains are expected to prioritize players from the local community ahead of those from
outside the community. As a community-based league, we emphasize the inclusion of
local players over non-local players.
3.7. Players are permitted to join or substitute for multiple community teams within the same
community, provided that all League and DUPR rating regulations are adhered to.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
3.8. Players must be at least 19 years old.
3.9. Players are responsible for verifying their paddle is on the current Approved Paddle List
(https://equipment.usapickleball.org/paddle-list/).
3.10. Any player found engaging in unsportsmanlike behavior, using illegal substances,
pretending to be someone else, or mistreating any player, spectator, or other person—
whether directly or indirectly—can be banned from the League. At the discretion of
League Managers, these players may also have their games forfeited. Please see our Code
of Conduct document in the LMS in the League Documents.

evidence.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
evidence.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor of 29 or below will be classified as “Not
Rated” (NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5.
This classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet
provide a suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-
established players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR.
Players classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most
appropriately reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches
and establish a more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged
to consult with a local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or
knowledgeable team captain for guidance regarding appropriate division
placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

Season DUPR Rating equal to the maximum individual DUPR rating allowed for
that division, minus 0.5. For example, in a division, where the maximum individual
rating is 3.8, an NR player would be assigned an initial Season DUPR Rating of 3.3

4.5.2. If a player is rostered on teams in multiple divisions, the highest adjusted Season
DUPR Rating assigned to that player will be used consistently across all divisions in
which they appear.
4.6. Team DUPR Rating Requirements: A team's DUPR Rating is calculated by adding the
Season DUPR Ratings of both players. Each division has established minimum and
maximum individual player ratings, as well as a maximum combined Team DUPR
Rating. These limits are strictly enforced.
4.6.1. Every lineup fielded for a match must comply with both the individual player rating
requirements and the maximum combined Team DUPR Rating for that division.
Teams that fail to meet these requirements will automatically forfeit the aƯected
games.
4.6.2. Games forfeited due to an invalid lineup will not be submitted to DUPR. The
League Management System will automatically record the forfeits and update team
records and league standings accordingly.
4.7. A player whose individual rating exceeds the Division maximum at the beginning of the
season is strictly prohibited from participating in that Division. If a Player rises above the
maximum during the season, they may complete that season in that Division.
4.8. A player whose individual rating is below the Division minimum at the beginning of the

evidence.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
evidence.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Point Scoring Methods
evidence.content:
5.3. Point Scoring Methods: Unless otherwise specifically stated, all games shall use
Standard Scoring as defined by the current USA Pickleball (USAP) Rules. Rally Scoring
shall be used only when a particular game or match format expressly identifies Rally
Scoring as the required scoring method.
5.4. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Match Setup and Roster Exchange
evidence.content:
5.5. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions
evidence.content:
5.6. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: DUPR Submission & Eligibility
evidence.content:
5.7. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Incomplete Matches
evidence.content:
5.8. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.8.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.8.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.8.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Coaching & Court Access
evidence.content:
5.9. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.
5.10. Spectator Interference: Spectators/non-participants must not be consulted on any call,
nor shall they influence any calls or decisions on the court.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Video Recording
evidence.content:
5.11. Video Recording: Video recording is allowed only if all players give their approval before
the game starts.
5.12. Rescheduling & Score Submission Deadlines: If both coaches agree, games may be
rescheduled to a diƯerent time on the same day or to another day within the same week.
However, all game scores must be submitted by the end of Sunday of the same week by

evidence.content:
midnight. If this deadline cannot be met due to weather conditions or other unforeseen
circumstances, the Home Captain must notify info@lwrpickleballclub.com before
Sunday at midnight with the rescheduled date and time. Failure to do so may result in
forfeiture of the games.
5.13. Makeup Game Deadline: All makeup games must be played at least one week before the
playoƯs/championship date.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages
evidence.content:
5.14. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.14.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.14.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.14.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
5.15. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.15.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.15.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.15.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.
5.15.4. Captains will form teams following regular season rules and Season DUPR ratings.
5.15.5. Players may participate in a Division end-of-season/Championship game only if
they have competed in at least one game within that Division during the current
regular season.
5.15.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.15.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.15.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.15.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

evidence.heading: LEAGUES
evidence.content:
6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the

6.1.9. Men’s/Women’s 9.1 Division: These divisions will initially be scheduled as a “flex
league” with matches initially scheduled for Fridays at noon but the Captains can
modify the match day/time (within 7 days).

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
6.1.9.1. This division will only have 2 lines (4 players) and require 2 courts.
6.1.9.2. Match Format: Teams play Round Robin. 2 out of 3 to 11 (win by 2). Plus,
potential Picklebreaker™ to 15. Teams will switch ends before Game 2. If a
third game is required, teams will switch ends during Game 3 when the first
team reaches six (6) points. Visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in
game 1 and 3. Each team receives one one-minute timeout/game.

the Picklebreaker™ format with the winning team collecting 1 additional point.
If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 1-point bonus.
6.1.9.4. Player Cap: Each player plays 4 games with a possible 6+ games.

6.1.9.6. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
6.1.9.7. The Picklebreaker™ shall be played only when the match is tied 2–2
following completion of all preceding rounds. The Picklebreaker™ features the
designated doubles teams that participated in the preceding rounds, rotating
in accordance with the Picklebreaker™ Rotation Rules. The Picklebreaker™
shall consist of one game to 15 points, win by two (2), using Rally Scoring.
Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not reflect
on individual’s W/L record.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.
Player Age Eligibility: A player’s age for league eligibility shall be determined by the age
they will attain as of December 31 of the current calendar year. A player is considered
age-eligible for the entire season even if they have not yet reached the required age by the
season’s start date.

evidence.content:
Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.
• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).
• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.
• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
evidence.content:
game by two (2) points. If the score becomes tied again, both teams shall again
become unfrozen. This freeze-and-unfreeze process shall continue as necessary
until one team wins the game by two (2) points. The game-winning point must
always be scored while serving.

evidence.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
evidence.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
evidence.content:
established order. The rotation process shall continue, as necessary, until the game is
completed and a winner is determined in accordance with the applicable scoring rules.
The Lineups: Captains determine the lineup order, making strategy an important part of the
game. They must decide whether to start with their strongest team or save that team for the
finish. The changing matchups shift the game’s momentum, while teammates cheering adds
energy and excitement that can help push a team toward victory.
With short doubles sequences and teams ready to rotate in quickly, the Picklebreaker creates a
tense, exciting finish to a full day of pickleball.

evidence.heading: TEAM ORDER & ROTATION
evidence.content:
1. TEAM ORDER & ROTATION
1.1. Captains will create doubles teams from the current players and designate play order
including abiding by all DUPR team rating/division rules.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
1.2. To determine the team that decides the serve, receive, side or defer options, use the 1 / 2
method or other mutually agreed option.
1.3. No time outs are allowed except for medical or equipment issues.
1.4. Optional End Change: Prior to the start of the Picklebreaker, both teams may mutually
agree to switch ends when the first team reaches six (8) points (15-point game) or thirteen
(13) points (25-point game). If both teams do not agree before play begins, no end change
shall occur during the entire game.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
1.5. The next teams in play order should warm up and be ready near the Picklebreaker court.
They should track the game score to ensure a smooth switch.
1.6. Teams have 20 seconds to complete the team switch. Time starts when the exiting team
has the ball to give to the incoming team.
1.7. The outgoing team must communicate the complete score and serve side before exiting.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content: 1.8. Substitutions do not require matching gender/side if it’s a mixed doubles setup.
